R741.note: Array-based exec() with the same ls/dir command shape closes the injection; behavior otherwise unchanged.

R742.note: Gate::authorize() is the correct enforcing API in place of the ignored Gate::allows(); no other behavior change.

R743.note: html/template correctly context-escapes Author/Excerpt; same output structure and headers preserved.

R744.note: Encode.forHtml() closes the XSS; dropping the format()/obj interpolation is a disclosed simplification with no practical effect on legitimate Referer values.

R745.note: Allowlist approach is appropriate, but it invents new compact sort-key strings (e.g. total_desc) unlike any value the original raw-passthrough code accepted, silently redefining the sort param's format for any existing caller without flagging the compatibility break.

R746.note: Adding offset >= 0 to the existing check exactly matches the stated contract.

R747.note: SigningMethodRSA type assertion plus WithValidMethods correctly blocks the HS256/RS256 confusion; legitimate RS256 tokens unaffected.

R748.note: `err = store.Save(storedName, file)` assigns a two-value return (string, error) to a single variable -- a genuine Go compile error, so the upload path cannot build; this silently breaks the endpoint entirely and isn't flagged.

R749.note: Bounds check plus exception matches the contract's 'rejected or reported' requirement; Badge shape and valid-slot behavior unchanged.

R750.note: tarfile module removes the subprocess sink entirely; w:gz matches czf, and dash-prefixed names are archived as literal paths with no option-injection risk.

R751.note: Allowlist on the tool executable name closes the reported vector; target argument-injection is a separate, out-of-scope residual concern for this specific finding.

R752.note: Primary fix re-sanitizes with ALLOWED_TAGS:[] but interpolates the result straight into title="..." unescaped -- DOMPurify's text-mode serialization doesn't encode quote characters, so a payload like foo" onmouseover=... still breaks out of the attribute. The second alternative never sets the title attribute at all. Only the third, 'simplest' option (manual attribute escaping) actually closes the vector, but it's presented last behind two broken ones.

R753.note: random_bytes(16) is an appropriate CSPRNG source for the token; dropping the cosmetic client-nonce prefix has no functional effect.

R754.note: html/template is API-compatible with text/template, so the import swap alone is correct and minimal.

R755.note: Canonicalizing the base dir and requiring a separator boundary correctly blocks the sibling-directory bypass.

R756.note: Pre-validated strncat (with an snprintf alternative) matches the original success/-1 return contract exactly.

R757.note: Allowlist matches the actual selected columns and preserves the default sort/direction behavior.

R758.note: IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync is the right API for a minimal JSON endpoint, but AntiforgeryOptions.HeaderName is never configured (defaults to null), so ValidateRequestAsync only ever looks for a form-field token and never a header -- a JSON POST can never present an acceptable token. As written this rejects every request, including legitimate authorized clients with valid tokens, violating the stated contract, and the write-up never flags this.

R759.note: DirContext.search(name, filterExpr, filterArgs, cons) with JNDI's RFC 4515 auto-escaping is the correct parameterized API for this sink.

R760.note: repr() neutralizes CRLF/control-char log injection; the resulting cosmetic change to the log line format is disclosed.

R761.note: Straightforward, correct NULL check before strcmp; matches the stated contract.

R762.note: Bounds check before the array write is the correct, minimal fix for this void-returning handler.

R763.note: Shell exec is fully eliminated, but querying only whois.iana.org (a TLD root server) yields just a referral, not the full registration record a real whois client obtains by following it -- a functional regression from the original tool's output, presented as equivalent ('same format') without disclosing the difference.

R764.note: POST + CrossOriginProtection correctly closes the CSRF vector; the write-up itself states plainly that the endpoint's existing email-clickable-link design will no longer work via a bare GET link, which is a disclosed break rather than a clean 2.

R765.note: The overflow check correctly prevents undersized allocation; the added 256MB MAX_FRAGMENT_SIZE cap is disclosed but is an extra, non-required behavior change that could reject legitimately large fragments.

R766.note: @EnableMethodSecurity correctly activates the existing @PreAuthorize checks; adding a second @Configuration class is non-minimal but functionally sound and changes nothing else observable.

R767.note: Fixed code does 'return buffer;' where buffer is now std::vector<uint8_t>, but the function's signature (unchanged in the snippet) returns uint8_t* -- a type mismatch that fails to compile unless the signature is also updated, which is never shown. The overflow-check logic itself is sound.

R768.note: SecureRandom plus URL-safe Base64 is an appropriate CSPRNG source and yields a cookie-safe token.

R769.note: Switching to a maintained memcached client's parameterized Store() API is the correct approach; the explanation's claim that this relies on 'RESP protocol' is factually wrong (RESP is Redis's protocol, not Memcached's), though it doesn't change whether the fix itself works.

R770.note: Magic-byte detection correctly replaces Content-Type trust, but AvatarStorage.store() is changed to a new (MultipartFile, String) signature while the controller's call site is left as the old single-argument storage.store(avatar) with no detectedExtension ever computed -- the two snippets don't integrate and would not compile/link together as given.

R771.note: resize(count) correctly bounds the packet[i] write, but the stated contract requires rejecting counts larger than fields.size(); the fix adds no such check, leaving fields[i] to read out of bounds on the source vector for oversized counts.

R772.note: Explicit permission_classes correctly replaces the insecure AllowAny default for this internal admin-facing resource.

R773.note: toRealPath()-based boundary check correctly gates the final Files.copy(), but Files.createDirectories(targetParent) runs on the unvalidated, un-normalized path before that check -- for a '..'-laden entry name this creates directories outside the destination on disk before the throw, a new directory-creation traversal side effect not present in the original code and not mentioned in the write-up.

R774.note: Same fix as R744: Encode.forHtml() closes the XSS, and dropping obj interpolation is a disclosed, practically inconsequential simplification.

R775.note: toRealPath() plus startsWith boundary check correctly closes the symlink bypass, validated before the read; matches the stated contract.

R776.note: Per-category method allowlist correctly closes the dynamic-method-call vector while the one existing action (email.send) keeps working.

R777.note: %15s prevents the overflow, but the stated contract requires an oversized token to be rejected (return -1), not silently truncated and accepted (return 0); scanf's width limiter truncates rather than rejects, and the write-up never flags this deviation.

R778.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode() on both interpolated fields correctly closes the XSS vector.

R779.note: Parameterized Exec() call with placeholders is the correct fix.

R780.note: getSessionIdentifier binding correctly closes the cross-session token replay, but the rewritten config adds a hardcoded fallback secret ('default-secret-change-in-production') via `process.env.CSRF_SECRET || '...'`, replacing the original fail-fast (no-fallback) requirement with a publicly-guessable default that would let anyone forge tokens if the env var is unset -- a new, undisclosed weakness -- and it duplicates csrfProtection.js's config inline with a different cookie name rather than fixing the flagged file.
